2: The patient's symptoms of flank pain, dysuria, and hematuria, combined with the imaging findings of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder and a soft-tissue-density lesion with calcific specks, are suggestive of a bladder tumor. The presence of a well-defined lesion with heterogeneous enhancement on CT also supports this diagnosis.

The imaging findings of a polypoidal lesion in the bladder with tiny hyperechoic foci and a soft-tissue-density lesion with calcific specks are also consistent with a diagnosis of papillary urothelial carcinoma, a type of bladder cancer.
